sections.html:
Columbia County deeds go to the Register and Recorder's Office at 35 West Main Street, Bloomsburg, PA 17815. Call 570-389-5632. That office also handles wills and estates, but a home sale only touches the Recorder of Deeds side.

The office posts three documents on its website: a fee schedule, a realty transfer tax policy and a list of recording requirements. Landex online access is available for searching records. Whoever assembles your closing package, whether a title agent or your own agent, should read all three, since a deed that breaks one rule comes back for correction.

Bloomsburg is the county seat, and it is where couriers and title agents bring Columbia County closing paperwork.

The schedule effective November 17, 2025 puts a deed or mortgage at $87.75. Each of those fees already folds in a $3.00 Recorder Improvement Fund charge and a $2.00 County Improvement Fund charge, and amounts marked with two asterisks include the state surcharges added under Act 45.

Columbia County recording fees by document type
DocumentRecording fee
Deed, corrective deed, deed of distribution$87.75
Mortgage, re-recorded deed or mortgage$87.75
Satisfaction or release of mortgage$59.75
Assignment of mortgage, easement, right of way$59.75
Power of attorney, affidavit, lease$18.50
UCC filing$100.00
Name search$20.00
Copies, per page (8.5 x 11 or 8.5 x 14)$0.50

Deeds and mortgages pick up extras: $1.00 for every name past four, $1.00 for each tract after the first, and $4.00 for every page past four. Other instruments charge 50 cents, 50 cents and $2.00 for the same things. A military discharge is recorded free. If the office mails a document back for fixes, it adds a $2.00 service charge.

Plan on three payments. The fee schedule calls for two separate checks for realty transfer tax, each equal to 1 percent of the sale price or fair market value, with the recording fee paid on top.

Pennsylvania's tax is 1 percent at the state level, collected by the county recorder along with an optional local tax. Buyer and seller are jointly liable. The recorder sends the state portion to the Department of Revenue, and local governments may divide their portion between school districts and municipalities. If land lies in more than one municipality, the deed must state what percentage of the tax belongs to each.

When the full tax is not being paid, a Statement of Value form goes in place of the check. Fill it out completely, and write out any claimed exemption along with the reason. The price has to read the same in words and in numbers.

sections.h2: What the recorder requires on a deed
sections.html:
The county's checklist is labeled a partial list of twenty items. These are the ones most likely to decide whether a house deed gets accepted.

  • Signatures and initials must be original, with blue ink preferred.
  • The document needs a date, and the acknowledgment cannot be dated earlier.
  • The acknowledgment has to be a formal one, not "sworn and subscribed," and include state, county, date, name, notary signature, stamp and expiration date.
  • A deed carries the buyer's Certificate of Residence or exact address, signed in original ink.
  • Anyone signing under a/k/a names signs each one, and each appears in the acknowledgment.
  • Foreign language documents come with an English translation.
  • Pages can be up to 8.5 by 14 inches, except maps. No margin rules apply because the office attaches a cover sheet to every document.

Mail-in packages need a stamped, self-addressed return envelope big enough for the contents. Maps must be signed and acknowledged by the owners. Subdivision plans need county or municipal approval and must be recorded within 90 days of it. The office does not take mylar.

A name search is $20.00, and copies are $0.50 a page on 8.5 by 11 or 8.5 by 14 paper or $1.00 on 11 by 17. Certifying Recorder of Deeds documents costs $1.50.

Errors can be fixed, though the process is strict. Re-recording a deed takes the original document with its original recording cover sheet, a written reason, and a new acknowledgment. When the original notary is unavailable, the parties sign again in front of a different one. Mortgages follow similar address rules: the lender's Certificate of Residence or exact address goes on a mortgage, and the assignee's goes on an assignment.

A corporation, partnership or other entity signs through an authorized officer. That person's title and company name appear under the signature and again in the acknowledgment.

The county had an estimated 66,193 people in July 2025, up 2.3 percent from the 2020 base. Bloomsburg (14,855 in 2010) and Berwick (10,477) are the two largest communities. The county covers 483 square miles along the Susquehanna River in central Pennsylvania, with farmland and state game lands across much of it.

There were 30,065 housing units, and 69.5 percent of occupied homes are owner-occupied. The median owner-occupied value is $206,200, median gross rent is $943 and median household income is $64,644. The county issued 111 building permits in 2025, which points to a market with steady activity.

When you price your home, a title agent or local agent can tell you how your borough compares. Bloomsburg, Berwick, Catawissa, Millville, Benton and Orangeville are the main places buyers search.

Begin with the title company or attorney running your closing and ask who will deliver the deed to Main Street in Bloomsburg.

  • Confirm the November 17, 2025 fee total for your deed's page and name count.
  • Write two transfer tax checks of 1 percent each, plus a check for the recording fee.
  • Check that the notary block names the correct county and shows an unexpired commission.
  • Attach the buyer's Certificate of Residence, signed in ink.
  • Enclose a self-addressed stamped envelope if the package is mailed.

Inherited houses may be exempt. Property passing by will or intestate succession is exempt from the transfer tax, and the county requires a Statement of Value to document the exemption.

A deed that is rejected delays the buyer's title, so build in a day or two for corrections. Phone 570-389-5632 with questions before you send anything. If the sale is a cash deal with a quick closing, the same recording rules apply, so have the notary block and the buyer's address certificate ready ahead of time instead of fixing them after the signing, since a notary has to be present again for any new acknowledgment.

faqs.q: What is Columbia County's base charge for a deed?
faqs.a: A deed or mortgage is $87.75 under the schedule effective November 17, 2025. Names, tracts and pages past the limits add $1.00, $1.00 and $4.00 each.

faqs.q: Does Columbia County want one check or several?
faqs.a: Two checks for transfer tax, each for 1 percent of the sale price or fair market value, and a third for the recording fee. The county's fee schedule requires the two separate tax checks.

faqs.q: Does Columbia County require a Certificate of Residence on a deed?
faqs.a: Yes. Each deed carries the buyer's Certificate of Residence or exact address, signed in original ink.

faqs.q: Can I mail a deed to the Columbia County recorder?
faqs.a: Yes, if the package meets every recording requirement and includes a stamped, self-addressed envelope large enough for the return. Send it to 35 West Main Street, Bloomsburg, or call 570-389-5632.

faqs.q: How soon must a Columbia County subdivision plan be recorded?
faqs.a: Within 90 days of its approval date. The plan needs county or municipal approval, and mylar is not accepted.
